title: Successor triangle for the canonical integral reduction tower
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, a scheme X and the completed integral coefficient sheaf B [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let P be a K-flat complex of B-modules [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Choose any finite-field datum D of characteristic different from l as required by the existing tower interface. Let F_n be the restriction to B of P tensor^L_B (O_E/(pi^(n+1)))_X, with the actual canonical quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower, lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined]. For every n>=0, there exist maps making F_0 --> F_(n+1) --> F_n --> F_0[1] a distinguished triangle, and its second arrow is precisely the canonical transition of F.

source.place: Tag 0942, lemma-bounded, displayed ideal-filtration triangle; Tags 06YN/06YS, K-flat resolutions; derived.tex Tag 0152, short-exact-sequence triangle.

proof.text: Lift the additive principal coefficient sequences to completed-ring module sheaves: the projection is linear and multiplication by the constant uniformizer is linear. The faithful exact forgetful functor reflects short exactness. For f=pi and g=pi^(n+1), the kernel-cokernel exact sequence for a composite gives 0 -> coker(f) -> coker(fg) -> coker(g) -> 0, since g is mono. Identify these cokernels with C_0, C_(n+1), C_n using their short-exact presentations. The equality p_(n+1) followed by the quotient map equals p_n ensures that the second arrow is the actual quotient transition.

For a complex with flat terms, tensor this coefficient sequence degreewise. Use exactness of the site tensor functor to obtain a short exact sequence of complexes. The tensor-unit and restriction/sheafification isomorphisms identify coefficient tensors with the recorded ordinary scalar extensions. Their normalization takes x to 1 tensor x. Naturality follows by canceling this epimorphic quotient unit; this makes the comparison natural for differentials. The same cancellation, the identity between coefficient projections, and compatibility of the recorded reduction units identify the tensor of the quotient map with the actual tower transition.

The short-exact-sequence triangle gives the required triangle for a flat-term complex. For an arbitrary K-flat P, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution Q -> P. The existing reduction-comparison isomorphisms between the two K-flat resolutions Q -> P and id_P commute with the canonical transitions. Transport the triangle along them, including the shifted first isomorphism for its final arrow. This retains the second arrow required in the statement. Zero complexes, n=0, and the empty scheme obey the same constructions.

theorem integralReduction_successor_triangle
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{0}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules.{u, u} l E X) ℤ)
    (hP : @CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients.{u + 1, u, u + 1}
      X.ProEt inferInstance (essentiallySmallSelf.{u} X.ProEt) (ProEt.topology X)
      (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted.{u, u} l E X) P) (n : ℕ) :
    let F := integralReductionTower.{0, u, u} l E X D hl P
    ∃ (ι : F.obj (op 0) ⟶ F.obj (op (n + 1)))
      (δ : F.obj (op n) ⟶ (F.obj (op 0))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk ι (F.map (homOfLE n.le_succ).op) δ ∈
        distTriang (completedIntegralDerivedCategory.{0, u, u} l E X D hl)
